{{Short description|American mathematician (1930–1998)}}
{{Use American English|date=March 2026}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=March 2026}}
'''James J. Andrews''' (March 18, 1930 – July 28, 1998) was an American mathematician, a professor of [[mathematics]] at [[Florida State University]] who specialized in [[knot theory]], [[topology]], and [[group theory]].<ref name="fst">{{citation|title=Mathematics professor James Andrews |first=De Witt |last=Sumners |authorlink=De Witt Sumners |journal=Florida State Times |date=October 1998 |volume=4 |url=http://www.fsu.edu/~fstime/FS-Times/Volume4/oct98web/5oct98.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120819094237/http://www.fsu.edu/~fstime/FS-Times/Volume4/oct98web/5oct98.html |archive-date=August 19, 2012 |url-status=dead }}.</ref>

Andrews was born March 18, 1930, in [[Seneca Falls, New York]].<ref name="fst"/> He did his undergraduate studies at [[Hofstra College]],<ref name="fst"/> and earned his doctorate in 1957 from the [[University of Georgia]] under the supervision of [[M. K. Fort, Jr.]]<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=James J. Andrews|id=507}}.</ref> He worked at [[Oak Ridge National Laboratory]], the University of Georgia, and the [[University of Washington]] before joining the FSU faculty in 1961. Andrews was a visiting scholar at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in 1963–64.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/frontpage?page=4 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130106144338/http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/frontpage?page=4|url-status=dead |title=Institute for Advanced Study: A Community of Scholars|archivedate=January 6, 2013}}</ref> From 1965 to 1967, he looked into [[cryptology]] research at the Institute for Defense Analysis, [[Naval Postgraduate School]], [[Monterey]], California.[https://web.archive.org/web/20120819094237/http://www.fsu.edu/~fstime/FS-Times/Volume4/oct98web/5oct98.html pg5] He retired in 1994,<ref name="fst"/><ref>[http://registrar.fsu.edu/9899general/retireda.htm Retired faculty], Florida State University General Bulletin 1998-1999, retrieved 2011-07-13. [https://web.archive.org/web/20120314041848/http://registrar.fsu.edu/9899general/retireda.htm Backed up to Internet Archive Wayback Machine]</ref> and died July 28, 1998, in [[Tallahassee, Florida]].<ref name="fst"/><ref>[http://www.math.fsu.edu/News/Math_Newsletter_Spr2000.pdf View from the Chair], Florida State University Mathematics Department, Spring 2000, retrieved 2011-07-13.</ref>

Andrews is known with [[Morton L. Curtis]] for the [[Andrews–Curtis conjecture]] concerning [[Nielsen transformation]]s of balanced [[Presentation of a group|group presentations]].<ref name="fst"/> Andrews and Curtis formulated the conjecture in a 1965 paper;<ref>{{Citation | last1=Andrews | first1=J. J. | last2=Curtis | first2=M. L. | title=Free groups and handlebodies | doi=10.2307/2033843 | mr = 0173241 | year=1965 | journal=Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society | volume=16 | pages=192–195 | jstor=2033843 | issue=2| doi-access=free }}.</ref> it remains open.
